newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Rebels stage fresh attack on Colombian pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Rebels stage fresh attack on Colombian pipeline.

text.p: Leftist rebels have staged a fresh attack on Colombia's already crippled Cano Limon pipeline, clouding the outlook for a resumption in pumping operations anytime soon, the state oil company Ecopetrol said Tuesday.
A company spokesman said the latest dynamite attack, the 38th this year, occurred Sunday in a rural area outside the city of Cucuta on Colombia's northeastern border with Venezuela.
"We can't do anything until the army moves into the area," he said.

Ecopetrol declared force majeure on two crude shipments totalling 750,000 barrels Monday because of the closure of the pipeline, which runs from the Cano Limon field operated by Occidental Petroleum Corp in northeast Arauca province to the Caribbean coast lifting terminal at Covenas.
A spokesman for Occidental told Reuters late Monday that the company was preparing to declare force majeure on the Cano Limon field itself, where the wells have been shut down since early Thursday.
The Ecopetrol spokesman said the closing of the wells was believed to have caused serious damage because of cave ins triggered by the loss of internal pumping pressure.
"It seems that there's been a lot of damage," he said.
He said guerrillas had claimed responsibility for the dynamite attack outside Cucuta but that it was not immediately clear which of the country's two major rebel groups had carried out the attack.
"There's no question that Oxy will have to declare force majeure on the field," the spokesman said.
